title: container-cuda-libmix-oom-timeline
content:
Scratchpad: container OOM + mixed CUDA runtime libraries (notes / timeline / commands tried)

Summary:
Observed intermittent GPU OOMs when bootstrapping the model server inside a Docker container (k8s pod). Symptoms looked like normal OOM at first, but further runs show weird library mismatches and occasional 'initialization error' from CUDA runtime. Hypothesis: a mix of system CUDA libs (host driver) and conda-provided libcudart/libcublas inside container + leftover LD_PRELOAD/ldconfig cache causing incompatible symbols at runtime. Also possible cgroup memory limits cause failure during heavy allocator initialization.

Context / environment:
- Host driver: NVIDIA Driver 535.54.03 on Ubuntu 22.04
- Node GPU: A100-SXM4-80GB (but repro also on RTX6000 dev laptop)
- Container base: nvidia/cuda:12.1-runtime-ubuntu22.04 (but app image pulls conda-packaged PyTorch built for CUDA 11.8)
- Torch: conda env pytorch 2.2.0+cu118 (built against libcudart.so.11.8)
- Serving runtime: local dev image with our runtime binary (rwd-runtime v0.14)

Timeline (abridged):
2026-02-18 10:12 - first failure seen during local k8s smoke test
- Pod logs: "RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 512.00 MiB (GPU 0; 79.00 GiB total capacity; 77.50 GiB already allocated; 1.50 GiB free; 1.00 GiB reserved in total by PyTorch)"
- Restarting sometimes fixes (suggesting transient allocation fragments)

2026-02-19 09:30 - reproducer run with strict logging
Command used:
  docker run --gpus all -e NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 -v /var/log:/hostlogs --entrypoint=/bin/bash my-image:dev -c 'python -u repro_load.py'

Observed output: (trimmed)
  >>> torch.cuda.is_available() = True
  >>> torch.version.cuda = "11.8"
  >>> ctypes.CDLL("/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcudart.so.11.0") succeeded
  Traceback (most recent call last):
    File "repro_load.py", line 42, in <module>
      model = load_sharded_model(...)
    RuntimeError: CUDA error: initialization error (9)

Notes: cdll loading of /usr/lib/.../libcudart.so.11.0 is alarming: container should not be referencing host /usr/lib, but the runtime FS had those libs present because of a mounted host path earlier (accidental).

2026-02-20 15:50 - ran ldd /opt/conda/lib/python3.8/site-packages/torch/lib/libc10_cuda.so\Command:
  ldd /opt/conda/lib/python3.8/site-packages/torch/lib/libc10_cuda.so | grep cudart || true
Output:
  libcudart.so.11.0 => /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcudart.so.11.0 (0x00007f...)

But conda pytorch expected 11.8. There is an older libcudart on the image that takes precedence.

2026-02-21 11:05 - tried quick fixes:
- Set LD_LIBRARY_PATH to /opt/conda/lib:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH (no effect)
- Ran ldconfig inside container to update cache -> pointed to /usr/local/cuda/lib64 which has 12.x libs -> error changed to undefined symbol: cudaGetErrorString when launching runtime (indicates ABI mismatch)
- Rebuilt image with conda-pack of pytorch + removed host mounts -> still intermittent OOMs

Error snippets collected:
- RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate X MiB (GPU Y; 79.00 GiB total capacity; Z GiB already allocated)
- RuntimeError: CUDA error: initialization error (9)
- ImportError: /opt/conda/lib/python3.8/site-packages/torch/lib/libcudart.so.11.0: version `CUDA_11.0' not found (required by /usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcublas.so.12)
- cublasGetVersion returned CUBLAS_STATUS_NOT_INITIALIZED
- undefined symbol: cuMemcpyAsync (when loading mixed libcuda/libcudart)
- [dmesg] Out of memory: Killed process 12345 (python) total-vm:xxxxxxxK, anon-rss:yyyyyyK

Commands tried (full list of interesting ones):
- python repro_load.py (worked sometimes fail other times)
- ldd checks: ldd $(python -c 'import torch, os; print(os.path.join(torch.__path__[0], "lib", "libtorch_cuda.so"))') | grep cuda
- readelf -s to inspect missing symbols in libcudart/libcuda
- env LD_PRELOAD=/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so python repro_load.py -> caused different crash (undefined symbol)
- STRACE: strace -f -e open,stat python repro_load.py -> confirmed the process opens /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcudart.so first (unexpected)
- ran with --gpus=all and without NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES (different device mapping but same behavior)

Hypotheses so far:
1) Library mix: application (conda) expects 11.8 but container image / host mounts expose older 11.0 libs or newer 12.x libs. The mismatched symbols cause failure in allocator initialization leading to sporadic OOM or init error.
2) cgroup memory / docker memory limits interacting with GPU allocator: if container memory is limited, the process might be swapping/pinned memory starved when building big CUDA context -> fail. Definitely seen dmesg OOM kills in some runs.
3) Device mapping: NVIDIA driver / container mismatch w.r.t. NVML versions causes transient device init failures (seen as init error 9).
4) Race in our serving runtime during shard load where multiple processes try to pin huge amounts of device memory simultaneously — makes OOM look like library issue.

Quick repro recipe (minimal):
- Build a small repro image that intentionally contains both /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcudart.so.11.0 and /opt/conda/lib/libcudart.so.11.8 and run the model load with verbose RTLD loading logging (LD_DEBUG=libs).
- Steps used:
  docker run --rm --gpus all -e LD_DEBUG=libs -e LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/opt/conda/lib my-image:debug python repro_load.py 2>&1 | tee ld_debug.log

Observed interesting ld output lines showing two different entries for libcudart and which soname gets bound per process.

Mitigations tried and notes:
- Force container to use conda libs by unsetting /usr/lib in PATH and LD_LIBRARY_PATH; still sometimes resolves, but not reliable for k8s nodes where host mounts happen via CSI driver (we mount nvml socket and the host has /usr/lib libs).
- Pin NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES and use driver-container-toolkit recommended runtime (no difference)
- Build and install pytorch from source inside container against native driver (painful but stabilized one test node) -> this eliminated the init errors but OOMs still occurred at high concurrency (likely real allocation pressure)
- Add retry + fallback (start smaller shards first, fallback to CPU for some shards) as temporary mitigation in serving runtime

Leads and next steps:
- Create minimal docker image that reproduces the mixed-lib scenario and share with infra team (ticket SRV-1123).
- Ask infra to ensure we do not mount host lib directories into app image (we found an accidental mount in CI job that includes /usr/lib)
- Add a diagnostic at runtime: print ldconfig -p | grep libcudart and run dlopen checks for paths (helpful for debugging customer cases)
- Consider shipping a sanity check in startup: verify torch.version.cuda matches the loaded libcudart soname (fail fast with clear error)
- Investigate allocator fragmentation: add TVM-style memory pooling, pre-reserve heuristics, and run workload with different batch sizes to map peak RSS/GPU memory relationship

Things to capture in minimal repro (for infra handoff):
- Dockerfile that copies both versions of libcudart into different paths
- repro_load.py that loads model shards concurrently (threaded) and logs torch.cuda.memory_summary() before/after
- LD_DEBUG=libs trace and full python stderr

Random notes / fragments:
- When the mismatched libcudart points to older soname, symbols like cuMemcpyAsync can be missing if host driver expects newer API (we saw undefined symbol)
- On one pod, I saw /var/log/nvidia-container-toolkit.log show "libcuda: mismatched soname" warnings (need to grab lines next run)
- dmesg line with oom-killer included cmdline -> useful to map which container was killed by PID

Immediate todo (short):
- [ ] Build minimal repro image and attach to SRV-1123
- [ ] Add startup sanity-check into runtime (LD lookup + soname check)
- [ ] Ask infra to audit mounts for /usr/lib on k8s worker images used for CI
- [ ] Run allocator-concurrency sweep: start N workers concurrently to measure threshold for OOMs

If anyone else hits this in the wild, useful first commands:
- docker run --rm --gpus all -e LD_DEBUG=libs my-image python -c 'import torch,ctypes,os; print(torch.version.cuda); print(ctypes.util.find_library("cudart"));'
- ldd $(python -c 'import torch,os; print(os.path.join(torch.__path__[0], "lib", "libc10_cuda.so"))') | grep cudart || true
- strace -f -e open,stat python repro_load.py 2>&1 | grep cudart

End of scratchpad.

Notes authored by: Ava Martinez (quick personal notes, to be converted into an infra ticket + focused repro)
